messages:
Priya Patel: Heads-up — I'm about to hand off primary for the night. We just got a few pages about increased 5xxs on the hosted inference API (region: us-west-2). I'm leaving notes here and tagging handoff.
Matt Nguyen: ack — what's the current impact? any customer-facing alerts?
Priya Patel: Small spike, roughly 1.2% of requests returning 503s over last 10m. No major customer alerts yet but a couple of errors surfaced in Support tickets. I've put a temporary rate-limit workaround on the low-tier route to protect capacity. :lock:
Jordan Lee: do we know if it's runtime (model-serving) or infra (k8s / node level)?
Sasha Rivera: based on the trace I pulled, the failures are originating from the runtime side; logs show repeated KV cache mismatches and OOM eviction on a subset of pods. That said node-level metrics show one host with elevated GPU memory errors. Could be both.
IncidentBot: INCIDENT CREATED: INC-2219 — 5xx spike in hosted inference (us-west-2). Severity: P2. Pageres: @eng-oncall, @eng-runtime, @eng-infra
Priya Patel: tagging @Jordan and @Sasha as primary/secondary for the rest of my shift. Jordan you take primary. Sasha you're secondary. I'll be reachable until 21:00 UTC then offline.
Jordan Lee: taking primary. I'll start by running the quick health check from the runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/oncall-handoff#runtime-503s
Matt Nguyen: runbook recommends checking pods with high restart counts and GPU memory metrics. Also try fallback to variant model (quantized) if runtime is overloaded.
Jordan Lee: copying commands I'm running now:
```
kubectl get pods -n redwood-runtime -o wide | grep us-west-2
kubectl logs pod/redwood-runtime-abc123 -n redwood-runtime --since=10m
rojobctl metrics gpu-memory --node node-42
```
Priya Patel: For immediate mitigation if it's runtime, roll traffic to the canary variant (v2-quant) or enable autoscale burst for Dedicated pools. If infra, coordinate with @eng-infra to evacuate node.
Sasha Rivera: I see repeated errors in runtime logs: "KVCache::miss -> fallback recompute -> OOM" at ~21:10. Patch idea: reduce max_batch_size for that model to reduce memory pressure. Also adding swap-like margin is risky on GPU.
Support Lead: got two tickets calling in “model responses failing intermittently, same prompt”. Customers unaffected in bulk but could escalate. I'm preparing a status blurb for support: short message and link to public status page if we need to announce.
Jordan Lee: I'm going to apply a temporary config patch to reduce max_batch_size from 64 -> 32 for the offending model deployment, and trigger a rolling restart across the pool.
Matt Nguyen: if you do rolling restart, do it staggered. Use the node-affinity to avoid killing all replicas on the same node. Also watch latency — smaller batch will raise per-token latency.
Jordan Lee: applying patch now. `kubectl patch deploy redwood-model-xyz --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"model","env":[{"name":"MAX_BATCH_SIZE","value":"32"}]}]}}}}'`
Sasha Rivera: I'm flagging a potential coverage gap: on-call schedule shows no infra secondary for this window (backup is on rotation but currently unassigned). Can we confirm who to page if node-level evacuation needed?
Priya Patel: noted — that's a known hole tonight due to PTO. I put an emergency contact in the runbook (oncall-rotations@redwood.internal) but we should escalate to eng-infra@pager if needed.
IncidentBot: @eng-infra requested. Pager escalated to infra on-call.
Jordan Lee: rolling restart started. Initial pods coming up with smaller batch size. Observing 503 rate dropping to 0.6% after 3 minutes.
Support Lead: updating affected customers: "We're investigating intermittent 503s in us-west-2; mitigation in progress. No data loss. We'll update within 30 min."
Matt Nguyen: good. Keep the mitigation for 15-30m to ensure KV caches repopulate. Also capture a heap/profile of the model process for postmortem.
Sasha Rivera: taking a memory snapshot and saving to s3: `s3://redwood-debug/2219999999/memdump.tar.gz`. Also logging current pod-node mapping.
Jordan Lee: 503s down to 0.2% and stabilizing. Removing temp rate-limit on low-tier route.
Priya Patel: thanks team — I'm handing off officially. Jordan primary, Sasha secondary. If anything node-level then page infra escalation path. I'll summarize in rotation doc before I go.
Support Lead: noted. I'll hold off customer-wide status until we confirm steady state for 30m. Will inform any premium customers in the next 10.
Jordan Lee: will keep monitoring. TODOs: keep mitigation for 20m, collect profiles, open INC follow-up with timeline and RCA owner.
Sasha Rivera: adding RCA owner suggestion: @Jordan Lee for immediate root cause triage; @Matt Nguyen for capacity/ktuning; @eng-infra for node investigation.
Priya Patel: thanks all. :wave:
Jordan Lee: ack, taking over. I'll post updates in this thread as things change."
